prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and for its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: Topological insulators are the strongest combination of conceptual originality, experimental confirmation and breadth in this shortlist. The Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant band insulators, the quantum spin Hall state and its observation in HgTe wells introduced a new organising principle for electronic matter that has spread well beyond condensed matter into photonics, acoustics and cold atoms. Seven of eight members ranked B006 in their top three, and four ranked it first. The theory-plus-decisive-experiment structure (Kane and Mele for the theory, Molenkamp for the transport observation) gives a clean and defensible prize that matches what is actually credited in the supplied names. Two decades of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and STM mean that maturity is not a concern.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is outside the credited set, and Zhang's death rules out a prize for him. Hasan's first ARPES observation of three-dimensional topological insulators is a real claim that a three-person limit forces us to leave out, and the 3D work also has contributions from Moore, Balents, Fu and others. The 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and topological phases also means a reviewer could ask how much new content this honours, although I think the Z2 and quantum spin Hall step in two and three dimensions is distinct from the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz work.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B006 first but proposes Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, a theory-plus-two-experiments configuration, while acknowledging that dropping Mele is a real fairness problem.
responses.response: I share the discomfort about omitting Mele, and I disagree with the resolution. Kane and Mele wrote the foundational 2005 papers jointly, including the Z2 invariant, so removing one of them while keeping an experimentalist on the 3D side is the harder choice to defend. The 3D case is itself a theory-plus-experiment story in which Fu, Kane and Mele predicted Bi-Sb and Hasan observed it, so Hasan's claim is partly already carried by the theory credit on Kane and Mele. I would keep the prize as a single, coherent achievement centred on the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant, and I accept that Hasan is the person most likely to be left out. If colleagues argue that the 3D observation is equally decisive, I would want that debated openly rather than settled by default.

responses.point: Pearce also ranks B006 first with Hasan and describes Mele as an equally strong co-originator of the Kane-Mele work, so the omission costs credit.
responses.response: We agree that Mele is an equally strong co-originator, which is why I include him. Our difference is on Hasan versus Mele, and I think the 2005 Kane-Mele papers are the single decisive step while the experimental realisations in 2007 (HgTe) and 2008 (Bi-Sb) followed from it. I would still ask Pearce whether a configuration that excludes a theory co-author in order to credit both experiments is consistent with how the committee has handled equal co-originators in similar cases.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first as a clean theory-plus-experiment story with the architecture underlying most superconducting processors, and notes that the Cirac-Zoller ion proposal is also strong.
responses.response: I accept that circuit QED is mature, original and technologically important, and I ranked it lowest on my ballot only because of timing. The 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is adjacent, and Girvin and others are outside the credited set, so the committee would be spending a second prize quickly on the same platform with an incomplete credit list. Technological impact through quantum processors is a strong point, but I do not think it outweighs the conceptual novelty of B006. I note that Johansson works on this platform and would raise the question of whether that connection should be weighed when counting first-place support for B038.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first because a clean theory prediction was followed by decisive experiments and a large new field of correlated moire materials.
responses.response: I agree that B017 has the cleanest credit structure on the list and that it is a serious alternative, which is why I include it. My reservation is maturity. The experiments date from 2018, and the origin of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated. Topological insulators, by contrast, have a stable interpretation after nearly twenty years. I would not be surprised if the committee prefers B017 in a few years, but I would not give it the prize ahead of B006 now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept omitting Hasan, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, from a three-person prize.
How much new content topological insulators carry relative to the 2016 prize on topological phases.
Whether the recent 2025 superconducting-circuit prize should be read as lowering or raising the case for circuit QED.
I rely on my own knowledge of the priority questions and have not verified them independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have no documented connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan or the other credited names, and my co-authors and supervisors listed there are not on the shortlist.
